name: Pawl
name_candidates: Pawl (the part of a ratchet that engages only when the mechanism tries to slip backward)
tagline: CI for the state your agent writes to itself: silent on pass, loud on block, never silent on hold.
stance: CI/CD for self-modifying agents, as corrected by the four lenses. Pawl is a harness-agnostic acceptance layer that (1) intercepts every persistent self-write at the file-path level (any tool, any thread, any harness sharing the directory), (2) judges the write against the incumbent on the user's own recorded sessions inside a sealed, host-side evaluator (paired, anytime-valid, tri-state, divergence-aware, sandbox-first), (3) keeps safety and cost as hard constraints inside accept(), (4) proves activation before it credits effect, and (5) makes every write revertible with depth > 1 and a verified round trip. It ships observe-only by default (change feed, load receipts, undo, spend meter) and turns blocking on per store; 'invisible until it blocks' is implemented one-sidedly: no cost or notification on the pass path, a loud block with an override path, and holds that expire or escalate rather than rot. It is not a proposer, not an LLM proxy, and not a 13th ledger format: it registers in seams that already exist (Claude Code hooks and plugin eval, OpenClaw skill_proposal_evaluate, Hermes pending queue and pre_tool_call, DSH tools/pre-execute + hook-protocol, pi tool_call/tool_result, Reef evaluate/decide) and emits one acceptance record as a profile over in-toto/EEE/OTel. What is genuinely new versus PACE/SEA/CAR: activation-eligibility partitioning that makes no-op evidence free, the incumbent's self-replay as the per-task noise floor and protected-corpus definition, an asymmetric disposition (fast BLOCK, provisional ADMIT, slow VERIFY with the same test continuing on live sessions), the measured middle case of The Replay Gap for harness edits, incident-seeded operational canaries instead of refusal probes, and one content hash joining write event, receipt, evidence, verdict and snapshot so undo, attribution, funnel alarms and the gate are one ledger.
thesis: Self-modifying agents already ship every mechanism except the one that decides. Proposers exist everywhere (Hermes background review and curator, Codex Memories, Claude Code auto-memory, Prime /refine, SkillOpt-Sleep, Meta-Harness, OpenClaw Workshop) and persist state on their own judgment; the honest statistical gates exist only on paper (PACE, SEA) and were validated on 0.5B-3B prompt edits with binary metrics; and users across ten issue trackers ask for receipts, diffs, undo, budgets and 'did it even load', never for statistics. The thesis: one append-only, content-addressed ledger whose entries (write event, load receipt, paired evidence, verdict, snapshot) share the artifact hash gives users the four things they ask for on day one (feed, receipt, undo, cost) and gives researchers the gate on day thirty, because the honest gate only becomes affordable when (a) evidence is partitioned by activation eligibility so that no-op edits produce ties at zero model cost, (b) the noise floor is measured for free by replaying the unmodified incumbent against its own sessions, and (c) the decision is asymmetric: confirmed regressions and safety violations are blocked from a handful of discordant pairs, no-ops are admitted provisionally, and lift is certified slowly by an anytime-valid test that keeps running on live sessions after admission. A gate built this way rejects most production edits 'for free' (which the null-effect literature says is correct), never starves the way SEA's gate did, and turns 'my agent modified itself' into 'the modification was intercepted, linted, sealed-evaluated, gated with error control, activation-checked, attributed, and can be reverted with one command'.
rsi_positioning: Pawl sits at the middle altitude of the Sept-2026 RSI discourse: harness-level, bounded self-improvement (Reliable-survey L2 scaffold / L3 improver; leezythu L0-L4; MetaRSI's Harness-RSI operator) with a frozen model, which is where every mass-market 'self-improving' agent and most 2026 papers live. It is explicitly the verification/acceptance layer, not a proposer: the surveys' shared verdict is that 'the acceptor is the weak link' (PACE: greedy acceptance = 30-42% false commits; HarnessDev: self-selection on visible feedback agrees with held-out on 34/64 switches; RSI-Exam: every frontier model loses 12-25% from visible to sealed), and the RSI survey (2607.07663) names 'governance-grade measurement of self-improvement' and 'trustworthy accumulation' as the emptiest areas. Pawl adopts the verification hierarchy as schema: every acceptance record carries the rung it was validated at (formal / execution / learned-judge / intrinsic); closed-loop acceptance is refused below rung 2; rung-3 evidence (cross-family judge) can admit provisionally but never certify; and any candidate that touches the evaluator, the gate, the protected corpus or the improver is an L4/L5 event that requires an independent anchor or a human merge (MetaRSI sealed-measurement invariant, dsh's trusted-branch rule, MLAS 'optimizer-optimizee collapse'). It also gives the other two altitudes something concrete: for Data-RSI/weight loops it is a drop-in decide policy for Reef (whose weight path defaults to AlwaysSelect) and a per-change version of RSI-Exam's sealed replay; for model-level RSI benchmarks it supplies the missing per-change gate, noise model and acceptor confusion matrix. Why RSI people care: all five 2026 surveys list the same four open problems (reference implementation of a gated update loop, regression/retention protocol, evaluator co-evolution without self-confirmation, multi-generation benchmark) and none ships code; Pawl ships runnable code for the first two, a benchmark for the fourth, and the mechanical-override + cross-family-judge + leak-scan machinery that is the practical (non-co-evolutionary) answer to the third. It is the thing that lets a lab say, with a signed record, what a loop is and is not improving. For adoption the word 'RSI' is dropped: to users Pawl is 'git + CI for the state your agent writes to itself'; the harness-RSI framing is reserved for the ICLR RSI workshop and the surveys' audience. Same code, two vocabularies.
what_evolves: Pawl itself does not evolve and is deliberately outside the mutable surface; changes to its evaluator, gate policy, canary set or protected corpus are L4/L5 events that go through a human-merged branch (dsh trusted-branch pattern). What it governs (the artifacts under acceptance) is:

SKILL.md bundles including references/, scripts/, assets/ (Claude Code .claude/skills, Hermes ~/.hermes/skills, OpenClaw Skill Workshop proposals and live skills, agentskills.io-format bundles, ECC/autoharness skill dirs)

Memory artifacts, the most-deployed and least-gated class: Claude Code auto-memory (MEMORY.md index + typed topic files, subagent/team stores), Hermes MEMORY.md/USER.md, Codex ~/.codex/memories, Prime memories, ECC instincts, ACE-style playbook bullets
Instruction files and rules: CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, project rules, Prime prompt notes and subagent specs in harness_state.json
Harness configuration the agent can write: settings.json hooks, plugin/MCP installs, OpenClaw config.patch, DSH cordis_define runtime plugins, pi/Prime refinements.jsonl entries

Loop-graph and code-level harness changes where a substrate exposes them (Reef native composition-tree nodes, Self-Harness hook slots, auto-harness agent.py), evaluated through the same candidate contract

Curator/consolidation operations that mutate several artifacts at once (Hermes curator absorbed_into merges, OpenClaw dreaming, Codex consolidation, OpenViking memory_diff) treated as one composite candidate with one snapshot
The protected regression corpus itself grows (new sessions become cassettes; incumbent stability is re-measured), but only by the recorder, never by the proposer
fitness_and_acceptance:
SIGNAL THAT DECIDES. The primary signal is a paired, per-instance, tri-state outcome (pass / fail / inconclusive) of the session's own terminal verification (the last test/build/lint command the user actually ran) re-executed in a git-snapshot sandbox, for incumbent vs candidate on the same recorded session ('cassette'). It is harness-owned by construction: the proposer never authored it and never sees it (HarnessDev score-path isolation; RSI-Exam fail-closed grader; SkillOpt#155's three binding requirements adopted verbatim: worktree is disposable state not a security boundary so real execution runs in a container with isolated credentials and no network, outcomes are pass/fail/inconclusive, execution is off by default). Secondary signals, each with its own decision rule: behavior change (first-divergence step vs the incumbent's own self-divergence), cost (tokens, wall-clock, artifact/context size), activation (loaded / read / followed), and safety (deterministic canary + behavioral canary). No LLM judgment is ever the final authority: PROCTOR's rule 'mechanical rejection overrides LLM approval, never the reverse' is hard-coded, and judge evidence is tagged rung 3 and can only produce ADMIT_PROVISIONAL, never VERIFIED.

DECISION RULE (builds on PACE, extended). Per candidate, eligible cassettes are visited in random order. Control arm = incumbent replayed k times (k=2 default, escalate to 3 on flake); these runs are cached and amortized across every candidate against the same incumbent. Candidate arm = 1 run first, more only if discordant. Each pair is classified concordant (tie), discordant-better, discordant-worse, or inconclusive (excluded from wealth, counted in the record). Ties are discarded and wealth updates only on discordant pairs (PACE's McNemar-style betting e-process, E *= 1 + lambda(2w-1), mixture over q in {0.6..0.9} as in our gate_power_sim.py), commit 'VERIFIED' at E >= 1/alpha with alpha=0.05. A second, harm-direction e-process runs on the protected corpus with alpha_harm=0.10 so blocking is faster than certifying. Per-task floor (synthesis claim 3, corrected): a task is 'protected' only if the incumbent passed it k/k in its own replay (observed stability, not assumed), and a candidate regression on a protected task counts only after k-of-n confirmation; our simulation shows why: on Bernoulli(0.6) tasks a k=1 floor false-blocks 93-100% of candidates, k=2 44-91%, k=3 13-43%, while real test-verified coding tasks are far more deterministic and the incumbent self-replay measures that per task for free. Run-level error across an unbounded candidate stream uses SEA's horizon-free CTHS schedule delta_k = delta_0 / (Z k log^2(k+1)), Z ~ 3.39 (the naive 1/(2k log^2 k) schedule over-spends 1.69x), and e-values across objectives are combined conservatively (all hard constraints must clear; cost and lift are separate e-processes; product only for independent constraints). Dependence from reusing cassettes across candidates is NOT covered by any theorem (PACE says the same of its dev set); mitigations are corpus rotation (new sessions arrive daily), agentdescent's rule that commit decisions read only full-eligible evidence and sub-samples may rank but never veto, and its kappa-style discount when a proxy judge is involved. Freshness (MetaRSI Eq. 22): evidence compiled before the last model-version or harness-version change is stale; control arms are keyed by model_served and invalidated on change.

DISPOSITIONS (the correction that keeps the gate on). VERIFIED (lift e-process committed, no floor violation, canary pass); ADMIT_PROVISIONAL (no evidence of harm after the per-candidate budget, default 8 eligible pairs or $0.50; the artifact goes live under continuing evaluation); HOLD (fewer than 3 eligible pairs or >50% inconclusive; the record says 'needs ~N more eligible sessions'; expires in 14 days into the policy default, never silently); BLOCK (>=1 confirmed protected regression, harm-direction commit, deterministic canary fail, lint fail, or 'evaluator unavailable' when the store is in blocking mode); NOT_ACTIVATED (candidate never loaded in any eligible replay; reported with the diagnosis: wrong store, truncated index, description outside matcher window). This asymmetry is the direct answer to SEA's ALG4, which accepted 0 edits at ~50 tasks and was switched off, and to the practitioner finding that a gate that rejects everything is disabled within a week; it is MGM/HGM's 'provisional admission plus posterior tracking' made explicit. Honest power statement from our simulation: with 20-40 binary paired tasks the gate detects a +10pp lift 11% (N=40) to 39% (N=160) of the time and a +30pp lift 98% of the time at N=40; so in practice Pawl reliably blocks regressions and safety violations, certifies only large lifts, and labels most production edits 'no-op so far' (consistent with CTA +0.3pp, SkillsBench 0 gain for LLM-written skills, Continual Harness 6.4% reuse, SkillOpt gains carried by 1-4 edits). Power is raised where possible with denser per-task signals (divergence step, steps-to-done, tokens) as secondary continuous objectives, and the test never stops: post-admission live sessions keep feeding the same e-process (this is the post-acceptance canary), and auto-revert fires on a confirmed regression.

NOISE. The Replay Gap (2608.08239) is taken as binding: replay is re-execution, never log-stitching; temperature 0 is not determinism (FP8 controls diverged 90-96%); every score is relative to the incumbent's own replay distribution; late fork points are safer and are preferred when a cassette has several verification points. Pure VCR replay is dead on real coding sessions (our own measurement: 50% workspace writes, 20% external, 13% nondeterministic calls; idempotent-only prefix 0-1 calls in every session), so replay is sandbox-first: workspace ops re-execute for real inside the git snapshot; externals and nondeterministic calls are served from the recording keyed by (tool, normalized input) via PreToolUse updatedInput / PostToolUse updatedToolOutput (verified on Claude Code 2.1.258, ~$0.007 per served replay) or plugin-eval mocks; the first call matching neither is the divergence point, and CTA's lesson applies: a divergence auditor must be calibrated against A-vs-A' before any divergence is attributed (CTA's detectors fired identically on no-change pairs). CAR's discipline is adopted: a counterfactual yields a distribution with CIs, abstention (HOLD) is a first-class outcome, and the incumbent must reproduce the recorded outcome before any candidate is credited (sanity floor).

SAFETY INSIDE ACCEPT(). Two boundaries per SafeEvolve/SkillMisevo (admission at write, revocation at reuse), because three exposures suffice and benign updates do not wash contamination out, so gating is per write, not periodic. Deterministic canary (zero model cost, any fail = BLOCK with a human override path): secrets/credentials/PII persisted into any artifact or .git/config (Hermes#101351), destructive commands in scripts/ (rm -rf, git reset --hard outside cwd; EvoMap#198), network egress in skill code, provider-boundary violations for memory jobs (codex#41711), session-specific facts entering global rules without a scope tag (ports, hostnames, absolute paths, dates), placeholder tokens codified as 'verified' (Hermes#89963), referenced files that do not exist, a revision that silently drops a verification/reversibility requirement its ancestor asserted (SafeEvolve's LLM-independent invariant), and 'rule contradicts the live environment' probes (arXiv 2609.11060 style, e.g. a skill asserting a command that returns 127). Behavioral canary (30-100 domain-conditioned probes, paired incumbent vs candidate, cross-family judge, mechanical override, ~50-100 model calls): seeded from the incident classes users actually file (learned helplessness / transient failure persisted, destructive action, credential persistence, permission-rule deletion, cross-user egress, fabricated completion claims) plus SkillMisevo-Bench, MemEvoBench and Agent-SafetyBench items for the refusal/injection axis. Probe text is never shown to the proposer, a held-out rotating subset guards against probe overfitting, and a confirmed new harmful behavior (2/2) is a BLOCK. Revocation at reuse: an admitted artifact retrieved in a new task family is re-canaried once before it counts, and attributed harm retires it.

TAMPERING VS OVERFITTING (two different fixes). Tampering (the one systems bug behind DGM#35, HyperAgents#39, HGM, AHE#15, SIA#36, autoresearch#599, pi-autoresearch): the evaluator runs host-side as its own process and identity; cassettes, snapshots, canary probes and gate state live in a store the harness's filesystem view cannot read (deny rule + separate uid where available, container mount elsewhere); every score is bound to a receipt sha256(evaluator version, cassette ids and hashes, candidate hash, snapshot ref, control-arm result hashes), DSSE-signed, and any number without a reproducible receipt is rejected; a leak scan rejects candidates containing cassette ids, test names, grader strings or probe text; 'evaluator unavailable' fails closed in blocking mode (DSH ApprovalOutcome semantics), with a loud alarm and expiry so fail-closed cannot become silent starvation. Overfitting via feedback (SkillOpt#154/#175): the proposer receives per-task pass/fail and failure excerpts but never grader source, regexes, rubric wording or verdict rationale; a mutation-content scan rejects quoted scorer tokens; 10% of accepted candidates are re-scored by an independent-family, rubric-blind judge with a divergence alarm; RQGM-style evaluator replacement is not attempted (OpenRQGM saw 0 replacements at 128 outcomes).

ACTIVATION AND ATTRIBUTION. Activation is a precondition of evidence, not a metric reported afterward (Lin et al.: skill-load 25% vs 96%, adherence .52 to .13; Anthropic's own plugin-eval docs: 'the most common first finding is a delta near zero with the tool_used: Skill grader failing'; Prime: 22/28 prompt notes and 63/69 memories never entered context). Per session, a deterministic receipt records for every artifact: resolved store path and hash, bytes available vs loaded, status complete | truncated | not_loaded | wrong_store, and load evidence (InstructionsLoaded, tool_use Skill, skill_view, resources_discover); eligibility for a cassette is computed from receipts before any model call, so a candidate that could not have loaded in a session is a tie at $0 and a candidate that loads nowhere is NOT_ACTIVATED with a diagnosis. Adherence uses mechanical predicates first (rules with checkable form: tool-order constraints, forbidden commands, required verification before commit) and a sampled cross-family judge only for free-text rules, offline. Attribution combines two arms honestly labeled: the unbiased arm is paired replay on replayable sessions; the observational arm is HGM-clade-style pooled outcome statistics per artifact over live sessions (activated vs eligible-not-activated), which is confounded (artifacts load on harder tasks) and therefore only ever produces 'keep / never-loaded / loaded-but-ignored / regresses / unknown-needs-N-more' recommendations, never a VERIFIED label. Retention and adaptation are reported separately (EvoHarnessBench BWT/FWT): a candidate can be VERIFIED on its target cluster and still BLOCKED on retention. Improvement claims that are to be published (research mode) additionally require AI2's matched-budget test-time-scaling control: the candidate must beat parallel-2 of the unmodified incumbent at the same rollout budget, with meta-agent tokens counted.

COST. Every record carries a cost envelope (proposer tokens if known, evaluator tokens, replicates, sandbox seconds, list-price USD), a per-store daily cap with a circuit breaker on repeated refusals or identical retries (Hermes#90446), and the sentence 'this gate cost $X' in every report; the corpus shows loops that do not print their own cost get disabled (codex#19105, claude-code#71633, darwin-skill#25).
core_technical_insight: Activation-gated paired evidence on the user's own sessions makes an honest gate cheap enough to leave on, and one content hash makes the gate, the undo, the funnel and the attribution the same ledger. Concretely: (1) An artifact's effect on a recorded session is a tie by construction whenever the artifact was not eligible to load in that session, and eligibility is computable deterministically from load receipts before any model call; since the e-process learns only from discordant pairs, the majority of production edits (near-zero effect per five independent 2026 results) are decided as 'no-op so far' at zero model cost, and a candidate that loads nowhere is diagnosed, not evaluated. (2) Replaying the unmodified incumbent against its own cassettes yields, for free and per task, the noise floor the entire field lacks (The Replay Gap's control arm), and it defines the protected corpus by observed stability rather than by assumption, which is what makes a per-task floor statistically well-posed. (3) Because regressions on protected tasks are discordant in the harmful direction, blocking harm needs a handful of pairs while certifying lift needs many; so the gate is asymmetric by design (fast BLOCK, provisional ADMIT, slow VERIFY) and the same anytime-valid test keeps running on live sessions after admission, which is why it never starves the way SEA's gate did and why post-acceptance canary and pre-acceptance gate are one mechanism. (4) Every entry (write event with provenance taint, load receipt, paired evidence, verdict, snapshot) is keyed by the artifact's content hash, so 'undo everything session X did', 'which artifacts came from that injected page', 'accepted=0 for two weeks', and 'was this ever loaded' are queries over one append-only ledger rather than four subsystems, and the acceptance record is emitted as a profile over in-toto/EEE/OTel so tooling that already exists can verify it. Competitors have the pieces (PACE the test, CAR the replay, Hermes the provenance, OpenClaw the hash-bound proposal, SkillOpt-Sleep the nightly loop) but none has the join, the eligibility partition, or the asymmetry, and it is those three that make the layer both statistically honest and adoptable.

Language-agnostic by construction so TypeScript substrates (OpenClaw, DSH, pi) and Python substrates (Hermes, Reef, SkillOpt) share one engine.

architecture.component: canary (deterministic + behavioral safety, pre- and post-acceptance)
architecture.responsibility: Deterministic probes (destructive commands, credential persistence, egress, provider boundary, scope leaks, environment contradiction) and a 30-100 item behavioral probe bank seeded from user-filed incident classes plus SkillMisevo-Bench / MemEvoBench / Agent-SafetyBench items, paired incumbent vs candidate, cross-family judge, mechanical override, held-out rotating subset. Post-acceptance: the same e-process continues on live sessions; confirmed regression or attributed harm triggers auto-revert to a known-safe checkpoint; re-validation once when an artifact is retrieved in a new task family.
architecture.interfaces: `pawl canary <candidate>`; probe bank as a sealed asset with hash pinned in receipts; revert trigger calls undo; alarms to report/review.

architecture.component: ledger (acceptance records as a standards profile) + funnel + spend
architecture.responsibility: Append-only JSONL, content-addressed, one record type per stage sharing the artifact hash. The acceptance record is an in-toto Statement v1 with a pawl predicate (candidate/incumbent digests, paired evidence in Every-Eval-Ever instance form, decision rule, verdict, disposition, activation, cost envelope, rung, evaluator id), also emitted as an OTel gen_ai.evaluation.result event with extension attributes. Funnel counters proposed -> intercepted -> linted -> evaluated -> accepted -> activated -> attributed plus a fifth 'ran vs reported ran' counter; alarms on accepted=0 over N runs, activated=0, held > threshold, unintercepted writes, spend > cap. Spend ledger reads each harness's own session logs (RSI-Exam budget.py pattern) and attributes tokens/USD to review, curation, replay and gate.
architecture.interfaces: `pawl report [--daily]`, `pawl status`, `pawl spend`; exports: aggregate-result.json (schemaVersion 1) so results ride Anthropic's report surface, OpenClaw evaluator envelope, EEE record, OTel event, DSSE bundle verifiable with cosign.

architecture.responsibility: Snapshot the whole learned-state tree (bundle dirs including references/scripts/assets, memory and index files) content-addressed before every unattended write; `undo --session X` (adds -> delete, updates -> restore, deletes -> recreate) with a conflict check for artifacts touched by later sessions; `restore <artifact>@N`; every snapshot round-trip tested before it is trusted; depth > 1; GC by policy. Replaces the field's broken per-tool rollbacks (Hermes#96962/#83580/#75228, OpenViking#4178).
architecture.interfaces: git-backed snapshot store under refs/pawl; `pawl undo`, `pawl restore`, `pawl snapshots`; used by canary auto-revert and by review 'reject'.

architecture.component: review (approval surface that does not rot)
architecture.responsibility: Batched (daily or threshold) digest with one-line summaries, full diff, evidence pointer, activation history and gate verdict; default disposition computed by the gate so humans review only HOLDs; holds expire into a stated default with a reason; scanner findings are overridable with a recorded justification (Hermes#94353 deadlock); surfaces where the user already is.
architecture.interfaces: terminal + markdown digest; OpenClaw Workshop board via evaluator findings; Hermes /skills pending diff/approve/reject; GitHub PR for team stores; optional push notification.

architecture.component: bench (acceptor benchmark on Harbor + ledger re-analysis)
architecture.responsibility: A Harbor task family that injects known-good / known-neutral / known-harmful edits (synthetic ground truth as in CAR and PACE's 'planted improvement among noise' and 'no-real-gain stochastic' regimes, plus real edits with hidden held-out outcomes and SkillMisevo/MLAS-style payloads) into a loop and scores the acceptor: false-commit, harmful-commit, missed-improvement, false-block on benign edits, evals per decision, safety decay, BWT/FWT, cost, vs a matched-budget test-time-scaling control. Plus an offline re-analysis harness for published ledgers (SkillOpt-Sleep evidence.jsonl, AHE change_manifest + git, Meta-Harness evolution_summary.jsonl, Self-Harness acceptance logs, Reef records).
architecture.interfaces: harbor task.toml family; six CLIs plug in as one-line adapters; results published as EEE records; `pawl bench run --gate {greedy|strict|pace|pawl}`.

integration_surface:
One core CLI, thin adapters, and a conformance suite that proves each seam does what its docs claim (does a deny stop the write, does a rejected proposal reach disk, does an evaluator timeout fail closed, does a promoted artifact actually load).

CLAUDE CODE (first adapter; the builder's own data). SessionStart: register session, snapshot workspace (HEAD ref + dirty patch under refs/pawl/snapshots), start cassette. InstructionsLoaded: record which CLAUDE.md / memory / skill files were injected and whether complete or truncated -> receipt. UserPromptSubmit: record the user turn and mark it trusted origin for taint. PreToolUse: (a) enforcement, `permissionDecision: ask|deny` for Write/Edit/Bash redirections into governed paths (memory dir, CLAUDE.md, .claude/skills, settings hooks) by unattended origins, with the write staged as a candidate; (b) replay, `updatedInput` to route a call into the sandbox worktree. PostToolUse: record tool results into the cassette; during replay `updatedToolOutput` serves recorded results for EXTERNAL / NONDETERMINISTIC calls (verified on 2.1.258, ~$0.007 per served replay). Stop/SubagentStop: finalize cassette, emit receipt, enqueue nightly evaluation. FileChanged on MEMORY.md and the fs watcher are the backstop for writes that bypass hooks. `claude plugin eval` as an alternative sealed backend: each cassette compiles to a case (scaffold_script restores the snapshot; history_file = transcript prefix to the fork point; graders = regex over the terminal-check output + tool_used asserting the test command ran + file_exists on artifacts; optional baseline grader vs the original transcript), run with `--ablation with-without`, `runs` = repeats, `--json` feeds the e-process; Pawl also writes aggregate-result.json (schemaVersion 1) so verdicts appear on Anthropic's report surface. Memory seam: PreToolUse on writes under the memory dir is the only acceptance point for auto-memory anywhere in the field; writes that arrive through internal paths are caught by the watcher and quarantined post hoc.

HERMES. Ingest tools/skill_ledger.py JSONL and .usage.json for the feed and activation; consume `~/.hermes/pending/{skills,memory}/<id>.json` when `skills.write_approval` / `memory.write_approval` are on and post verdicts (approve/reject through the same replay-through-skill_manage path with the gate-bypass token, so Hermes bookkeeping stays intact); register `ctx.register_hook()` plugin for post-turn review and curator events; shell `pre_tool_call` fail-closed for write_file/patch/terminal writes into ~/.hermes/skills and MEMORY.md by `background_review` origin (tools/skill_provenance.py ContextVar), which closes hermes#99729; treat curator consolidations (absorbed_into) as composite candidates with one snapshot; answer hermes#96704's RFC arms with `pawl audit` (activation arm from transcripts needs no model calls). 

OPENCLAW. A plugin registering `skill_proposal_evaluate` (event: proposal id/kind/revision/revisionSha256 + candidate and baseline BundleSnapshots with per-file sha256 and treeSha256; result: findings[]{ruleId,severity,message,file,line}, metrics, evaluatorVersion, mode:'baseline-comparison', decision pass|revise|block, decisionReason) — the first third-party implementation of the seam its docs wrote for 'external optimization loops'; HOLD maps to revise, BLOCK to block, and because only a completed `block` vetoes apply and errors/timeouts fail open, the plugin converts its own failures into `block` when the store is in block mode; consume `skill_proposal_changed` / `skill_changed` (before/after tree hashes) for the feed; `before_tool_call` (block / requireApproval) to cover `autonomous.mode: auto` direct edits that the Workshop admits bypass proposals; verdicts render on the Workshop board.

DEEPSEEK HARNESS. A dsh plugin on `tools/pre-execute` (typed PreToolDecision deny for writes into the learned-state tree by unattended actors; monotonic deny-only guard so listener order cannot resurrect a denied write), `tools/post-execute` (attach verdict context), `agent/turn-stopping` (finalize cassette), with `ApprovalOutcome` fail-closed on 'unavailable'; the Claude Code hooks.json runs unmodified under the `dsh-hooks-claude-code` bridge, so one command-hook adapter covers Claude Code, Codex and DSH; Cordis revertible effects give atomic revert for runtime self-modifications (cordis_define); publish as a marketplace plugin next to dsh-verify / dsh-verification.

PI / PRIME AGENT. pi extension: `tool_call` (block writes to governed paths), `tool_result` (serve recorded results during replay), `resources_discover` (report skill paths for receipts), `agent_end` (finalize). Prime: watch harness_state.json and refinements.jsonl -> candidates with before/after snapshots; render the diff before apply (prime#684) and hook `/refine rollback <id>` to `pawl undo`; the receipt exposes the alphabetical 6-entry head-slice problem (22/28 notes never loaded).

REEF. `pawl.decide` as a drop-in `decide` policy for harness recipes (anytime-valid paired + protected seed-suite floor instead of pooled W/L > min_win_margin; answers reef#356), consuming the recipe's interleaved candidate/incumbent episodes; `recheck_every` replaced by the continuing e-process; acceptance records emitted alongside releases; the acceptor benchmark converts to Harbor tasks per reef#447.

SKILLOPT-SLEEP. Implement the requested AgenticReplayBackend (microsoft/SkillOpt#155): worktree + container, tri-state, execution off by default; map evidence.jsonl to pawl.evidence; expose gate_no_regression as the k-of-n floor.

CODEX. PostToolUse block/replace and Stop (documented best-effort since some tool paths opt out); watch ~/.codex/memories; provider-boundary DLP rule for the memory writer (codex#41711).

Registries and standards (month 3): agentskills.io `evidence/` convention carrying the signed acceptance record and activation field; in-toto predicate proposal filed alongside #554; OTel gen_ai.evaluation.result attribute extension; EEE record profile with the selection denominator (candidatesCompared/candidatesCleared).

killer_demo: Five minutes on a Claude Code + Hermes user's laptop, nothing pre-arranged. (0:00) `pipx install pawl && pawl init`. Pawl backfills from transcripts that already exist and prints, in ten seconds and with no model calls: 'Found 212 Claude Code sessions (41 replayable with a terminal check) and 3 stores. CLAUDE.md: loaded complete in 212/212. Auto-memory: truncated in 9 of the last 12 sessions; the newest 6 entries (your corrections from Tuesday) never reached the model. 14 skills: 5 never loaded in 60 days; 1 loaded in 31 sessions and contradicted in 12 (rule: run pytest before commit). 18 unattended writes last week from Hermes background review, 1 of them bypassed skill_manage bookkeeping.' (1:00) Trigger one real Hermes background review (or one Claude session that saves a skill). Pawl intercepts the write before it lands, snapshots the tree, and the lint blocks half of it instantly: a placeholder 'HH:MM' codified as 'Verified 2026-09-14', and a hostname from this session entering a global rule without a scope tag. The rest is staged as a candidate with its diff, writer origin and taint shown. (2:00) `pawl gate cand_…` runs the sealed evaluator against the 6 cassettes where this skill is eligible to load (the other 35 are ties at $0): the incumbent's own replay is already cached (3/3 stable on 5 of 6), the candidate replays in a worktree container with externals served from the recording, and the per-task diff table appears: tri-state outcome, divergence step, tokens, versus the incumbent's noise floor. Verdict: BLOCK — confirmed regression 2/2 on cas_8a1 (the flaky-test session you fixed last Tuesday), incumbent stable 3/3, cost of this gate $0.31, one-line reason, an override path. (3:30) `pawl undo --session <the review's session id>` restores every file the review touched, including references/ and scripts/, and prints the verified round trip. (4:00) `pawl report` shows the week: '12 self-modifications: 2 verified, 5 admitted provisionally (no-op so far, $0), 2 blocked (would have regressed on your own past tasks), 1 blocked by canary (a token persisted into .git/config), 1 held (needs ~6 more sessions, expires Friday), 1 never activated: the memory index overflowed and dropped it — here is the line. Total cost $2.14. Undo any of these with one command.' (4:30) Switch to the OpenClaw Workshop board: the same verdict renders in the evaluator slot as findings + pass|revise|block, with a signed acceptance record that `cosign verify-attestation` accepts. The sentence that sells it is '1 never activated — here's why'; the sentence that keeps it installed is '$2.14'.
research_contribution: TITLE: 'Ties Are Free: Activation-Gated, Anytime-Valid Acceptance for Self-Modifying Agents, Evaluated on the Field's Own Ledgers and Sessions'. CLAIM (three parts, each with a number): (1) Re-analysis. Replaying the accept decisions recorded in published harness-evolution ledgers (SkillOpt-Sleep evidence.jsonl, AHE change_manifest + git, Meta-Harness evolution_summary.jsonl, Self-Harness acceptance logs, Reef records, community autoresearch results.tsv) under a sealed, paired, anytime-valid gate with a k-of-n protected floor and activation eligibility rejects a large fraction (target: >40%, the PACE band is 30-42%) of edits those loops accepted as indistinguishable from noise, and the rejected set contains the majority of the held-out regressions those papers report, at lower evaluation cost than their strict-held-out gates (sequential stopping + eligibility ties). (2) The Replay-Gap middle case. On real Claude Code and Hermes sessions, for edits proposed by real refiners (Hermes background review, Claude auto-memory, SkillOpt-Sleep), we report the first divergence-point distribution under sandbox-first branched re-execution with a same-configuration control arm: the prediction is that more than half of accepted production edits never change the action sequence on the user's own eligible past tasks, and that early divergence on previously-passing, incumbent-stable tasks predicts confirmed regression at a rate far above the control-arm floor. (3) Acceptor confusion matrix. On a Harbor-packaged benchmark that injects known-good, known-neutral and known-harmful edits (synthetic ground truth plus SkillMisevo/MLAS-style payloads, PACE's 'planted improvement among noise' and 'no-real-gain stochastic' regimes) into three loops (a SkillOpt-style skill loop, a memory loop, a Reef harness recipe), Pawl's gate dominates greedy, strict-held-out, Reef W-L margin, PACE-only and LLM-judge-only gates on the joint (false-commit, harmful-commit, false-block-on-benign, evals-per-decision) frontier while a matched-budget test-time-scaling control bounds what 'improvement' may mean. EXPERIMENT: offline ledger replay with the published per-task outcomes; online branched re-execution on >= 200 cassettes from >= 5 volunteer users (builder + hermes#96704 / SkillOpt#155 contributors), k=3 incumbent controls, cost accounted; benchmark runs with six CLIs via Harbor adapters, 5 seeds, BWT/FWT reported separately, safety decay via the canary bank with a held-out probe split. BASELINES: greedy keep-if-up (autoresearch, Meta-Harness), strict held-out no-ties (SkillOpt, Self-Harness, auto-harness), Reef pooled W/L with min_win_margin, PACE per-candidate e-process without floor/activation, SEA confidence-sequence gate, LLM-judge-only acceptance (SkillClaw-style), human approval queue (OpenClaw), and AI2's parallel-K / sequential-K test-time-scaling control at matched budget. FALSIFIERS: the claim is false if (a) held-out regressions are as frequent among edits Pawl accepts as among edits greedy accepts (rejection does not concentrate harm), (b) at equal false-commit rate Pawl costs more evaluations than the strict-held-out gate (eligibility ties and sequential stopping buy nothing), (c) the divergence point does not predict confirmed regression beyond the control-arm distribution (AUC <= 0.6), or (d) the incumbent self-replay floor is not stable across days/model versions so that 'protected' tasks flip in the control arm at rates comparable to candidate arms (the noise model is not a noise model). A secondary, cheaper result is the null-effect audit: on volunteers' stores the counterfactual lift of most LLM-written artifacts is indistinguishable from zero at matched budget, reported per artifact class.
adoption_path: Adoption follows the issue corpus, not the paper. Day 1 value with zero risk: `pawl init` backfills from transcripts that already exist, runs no model calls, and answers the questions users actually file (what changed since yesterday and from which session, did my memory load or truncate, which skills never load, undo what that background review did, what does the loop cost). Observe-only is the default and stays free on the pass path; hold and block are per-store opt-ins that users turn on after the digest has shown them a would-have-blocked. This is the one-sided invisibility the practitioner lens demands, and it puts the primitives in the order users demand them (feed/receipts, undo, provenance, cassette, hidden statistics, operational canary, sealed evaluator, benchmark). Second, attach where someone else pays and it runs off the hot path, which is the pattern that actually spread (ClawHub scanning, OpenClaw Workshop): the OpenClaw `skill_proposal_evaluate` plugin is the only substrate contract written for exactly this role and has zero third-party implementations, so the first real evaluator there is a visible win in a 389k-star ecosystem; the DSH marketplace already hosts verification plugins in this slot; Hermes has an open in-tree RFC (#96704) whose cheapest arm Pawl ships; SkillOpt's maintainers endorsed the exact replay backend (#155) and a contributor volunteered; Reef's decide policy is a one-PR integration with an open issue (#356) asking for it. Third, speak both languages: 'git + CI for the state your agent writes to itself' for users (no user issue says RSI), and 'the verification layer for harness-RSI' for the ICLR RSI workshop, the survey authors and the AI2/UW evaluation group; the same code and the same signed record serve both. Fourth, be the record, not the competitor: emit aggregate-result.json so verdicts ride Anthropic's report surface, the OpenClaw envelope so they show on the Workshop board, and an in-toto/EEE/OTel profile so registries (ClawHub, LobeHub, agentskills.io) can display effect evidence next to malware scans without adopting a new format; file the profile in the venues that have adjacent items (in-toto #554, OTel GenAI SIG, EvalEval) rather than founding a standard. Fifth, ship the Harbor benchmark and the ledger re-analysis so every harness-evolution paper has a reason to cite the gate and every maintainer has a number for their own acceptor. The trap to avoid is the one that killed SkillClaw and hermes-agent-self-evolution: an integration that works at the API level and breaks at the plumbing level (discovery paths, validators, deploy step). Hence the version-pinned conformance suite and the rule that Pawl never mutates a harness's config or intercepts its model traffic.

nearest_competitors.name: PACE (arXiv 2606.08106) — paired anytime-valid commit evaluation
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: PACE is the decision rule Pawl builds on (paired discordant-pair betting e-process, commit at 1/alpha) and it supplied the field's only acceptor-level measurement (greedy = 30-42% false commits). It has no code, is validated only on 0.5B-3B Qwen prompt edits with binary GSM8K/SVAMP/ARC metrics, controls only per-candidate error, has no per-task floor, no multi-objective, no tri-state, and no notion of activation. Pawl implements it in a harness, adds the harm-direction e-process and k-of-n protected floor on incumbent-stable tasks, cost as a second e-process, SEA's CTHS run-level spend schedule, tri-state outcomes, activation-eligibility partitioning (ties at $0), the asymmetric disposition set, and a continuing test after admission — and evaluates it on real sessions and published ledgers rather than a toy loop.

nearest_competitors.name: SEA (arXiv 2607.00871) — self-evolving agents with anytime-valid certificates
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: SEA's certificate schema (decision ACCEPT/HOLD/REJECT/NSF, delta spent, cumulative delta) and its horizon-free CTHS spending schedule are reused. But SEA's harness-edit gate (ALG4) accepted zero edits at ~50 tasks, cost ~90 min per round (13x the rest of the loop) and was switched off, while the components that moved the metric ran ungated. Pawl's answer is structural: evidence accumulates across many cheap rounds and across days on live sessions, no-ops are admitted provisionally instead of held forever, blocking is faster than certifying, and the expensive arm only runs on eligible cassettes. SEA has no public code; Pawl is a CLI.

nearest_competitors.name: Causal Agent Replay (arXiv 2606.08275) — counterfactual attribution by do-interventions
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: CAR supplies the intervention vocabulary (do_policy, do_context), the rule that a counterfactual is a distribution with CIs and an explicit abstain state, and the sanity floor (the factual run must reproduce before a counterfactual is trusted); all three are adopted. CAR is post-hoc failure attribution with mocked tools, abstains ~80% of the time on real traces, and its author's power analysis shows more rollouts cannot fix replay fidelity. Pawl is a gate, not a debugger: it re-executes stateful tools in a git-snapshot sandbox, treats abstention as HOLD with an expiry, uses the incumbent's own replay as the control distribution, and only spends rollouts on activation-eligible sessions.

nearest_competitors.name: The Replay Gap (arXiv 2608.08239)
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: A negative result Pawl takes as binding rather than a competitor: log-stitching replay scores the wrong world (3-8% valid states after early interventions, every success-relevant outcome mispredicted, T=0 not deterministic). Pawl's replay is therefore branched re-execution with a same-configuration control arm, prefers late fork points, and reports the divergence-point distribution for harness edits (a smaller perturbation than a model swap) as a measured object — the middle case the paper leaves open.

nearest_competitors.name: SafeEvolve / SkillMisevo-Gym (arXiv 2608.12851)
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: SafeEvolve is the closest thing to a harness-agnostic acceptance layer for one artifact class (SKILL.md): admission audit at write plus revocation at reuse, a GovernableStore proven across Claude Code/Codex/OpenClaw/Hermes, and the LLM-independent invariant that a revision may not drop an ancestor's verification requirement (reused verbatim). It is post-hoc governance with the same-model critic as the evolving backbone, judges artifact content rather than outcomes, costs ~13pp carryover utility, and barely beats a static scanner on fresh-session harm. Pawl puts safety inside accept() as a hard constraint with a mechanical override, seeds probes from the operational incident classes users actually file (destructive action, credential persistence, egress, permission-rule deletion) rather than refusal alone, uses a cross-family judge, covers memory/rules/config as well as skills, and pairs the safety term with an outcome gate so utility cost is measured, not assumed.

nearest_competitors.name: Reef (Human-Agent-Society) — continual-learning release pipeline
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: Reef is the most likely first institutional adopter, not a rival: its propose -> paired-evaluate -> decide recipe contract, versioned releases and canary/shadow routing are exactly the lifecycle Pawl's verdicts feed. Reef's gate is a pooled W/L tally over a tiny task suite with one-step rollback and AlwaysSelect for weights (#356); it is an LLM proxy that requires repointing model traffic and has no protected seed-suite floor, no activation check, no per-session receipts and no cross-harness ledger. Pawl ships as a Reef decide policy and Harbor conversion, and separately runs on hooks/plugins where a proxy is unacceptable (SkillClaw's fate: 'broke the harness', 'deprecated').

nearest_competitors.name: SkillOpt-Sleep (Microsoft) — nightly skill evolution with a strict held-out gate
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: SkillOpt-Sleep is a proposer plus gate coupled to one artifact type: strict-improvement on a val-slice mean (per-task regressions accepted; gate_no_regression opt-in), an optimizer that copies judge regexes into skills (#154/#175), and a replay backend its maintainers want but do not have (#155). Pawl is gate-only, proposer-agnostic, evaluates any writer (Hermes review, Claude auto-memory, Prime refine) on the user's own sessions, keeps grader text away from the proposer, adds the per-task floor as a default, and implements the AgenticReplayBackend #155 asked for under its three constraints.

nearest_competitors.name: agentdescent (Birfy) — Beta-posterior acceptance with regression guard
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: agentdescent treats the gate as the load-bearing component and contributes rules Pawl reuses: commit decisions read only full-eligible evidence (sub-samples rank, never veto), discount evidence counts by kappa when a proxy judge is involved and bind the rectifier to a verifier version, freeze the oracle by name. It is an in-process Python engine coupled to its own types, its default oracle is tautological, blast radius is declared not estimated, and there is no post-commit monitoring, canary or rollback. Pawl is an out-of-process CLI with a sealed evaluator, a measured (not declared) impact surface via receipts, and post-admission continuation with auto-revert.

nearest_competitors.name: auto-harness (NeoSigma) — gating.py exit 0/1 with PROGRAM.md
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: auto-harness proved the right interface shape (a dumb CLI with exit codes, any coding agent as the optimizer, an abstract run(task_ids) -> reward) and Pawl copies that shape. But its gate state (best score, regression suite, config, PROGRAM.md) lives inside the agent-writable surface, acceptance is single-run tie-accepting on ~27 tasks, and trace isolation is enforced in the file the agent edits. Pawl keeps gate state host-side and sealed, hashes the split and evaluator into receipts, and replaces the monotone ratchet with paired sequential statistics.

nearest_competitors.name: Hermes Agent (Nous) — skill_manage guards, ledger, write_approval
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: Hermes is the largest deployed self-writer and the best negative-result corpus: write-origin provenance, ownership/pin guards, read-before-write, a fail-closed ledger and a staged approval queue all held up in production, while every prompt-level quality rule was bypassed and the loop was silently dead for weeks (#95976) and the approval queue rotted (#105770). Hermes's ledger is 'telemetry, not a gate' and none of it is portable. Pawl consumes Hermes's pending queue, ledger and provenance, adds the missing verdict, receipts, funnel alarms, undo that restores whole bundles, and path-level enforcement that closes the write_file/patch bypass (#99729).

nearest_competitors.name: Prime Agent /refine (Prime Intellect)
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: Prime's typed, versioned harness_state.json with before/after snapshots and refinements.jsonl is a good candidate substrate, but acceptance is the refiner's own judgment, expectedOutcome is free text never checked, the overview injects an alphabetical 6-entry head slice so most entries never enter context, and '/refine is invisible' was closed unfixed. Pawl turns each refinement into a candidate with a checked expected_effect, shows the diff before apply, emits the load receipt that reveals the head-slice bug, and gates on outcomes.

nearest_competitors.name: DeepSeek Harness (dsh)
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: dsh ships the best-specified attachment map in the field (typed pre-execute decisions, deny-only guards, fail-closed ApprovalOutcome, revertible Cordis effects, a session log with model-visible <=> logged) and explicitly deferred the evaluator 'until its authority, isolation, and provider contract are designed'. Pawl is that contract, implemented as a dsh plugin, and because dsh runs Claude Code/Codex hooks.json unmodified, one adapter covers three harnesses.

nearest_competitors.name: OpenClaw Skill Workshop + `claude plugin eval` (vendor measurement tooling)
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: OpenClaw's proposal-first, hash-bound, event-ledgered Workshop and Anthropic's with/without plugin eval are the vendor pieces Pawl plugs into rather than competes with: the Workshop has an evaluator seam with zero third-party implementations and fail-open semantics, checks only safety regexes and hashes, and defaults to ungoverned auto; plugin eval has no paired statistics, no sealed split, a haiku judge by default, and lets the proposer author its own cases. Pawl is the first Workshop evaluator, wraps plugin eval as a sealed backend with cassette-derived graders the proposer cannot edit, and emits both vendors' formats.

risks: Replay fidelity and power: even sandbox-first re-execution diverges from itself (T=0 is not determinism; provider model updates mid-week invalidate control arms), so the protected corpus may be small and lift certification rare; if fewer than ~20 stable, eligible cassettes exist per user the gate is mostly a regression/safety detector, which must be stated honestly rather than sold as fitness.

Hooks are bypassable: Codex documents that some tool paths opt out, Hermes write_file/patch reach the skills dir directly, OpenClaw auto mode skips proposals, and Claude Code auto-memory may write through internal paths; until harnesses expose rooted write surfaces, enforcement is best-effort plus post-hoc quarantine, and a bypass in block mode is a silent hole unless the watcher alarm is loud.

Adapter churn is the real cost: Hermes shipped 947 commits in four days, OpenClaw breaks plugins per release, Claude Code's memory slug is unstable across versions; a 1-3 person team can keep at most three adapters conformance-green at a time, so sequencing (Claude Code, OpenClaw, Hermes first) and a pinned conformance suite are load-bearing.

Cost on paid plans: sandbox replays spend real model tokens (tens of thousands per cassette arm); without eligibility ties, early stopping, cached incumbent arms, per-store caps and a printed cost line the loop will be disabled exactly as Codex Memories and skill-creator evals were.

Fail-closed can become starvation: 'evaluator unavailable = reject' in block mode is correct for integrity but reproduces the approval-queue rot users hate unless holds expire loudly, defaults are computed, and observe mode remains the default.

Goodhart of the gate itself: a proposer that sees pass/fail per task can still learn to satisfy the protected corpus or the canary bank; sealing cassettes and probes, rotating held-out subsets, never exposing rationale, and leak-scanning candidates reduce but do not eliminate this, and the field has no seeded testbed for gate-gaming yet (we build one in month 3).

Statistical honesty under reuse: cassette reuse across candidates creates dependence no theorem covers; corpus rotation and the full-evidence invariant mitigate it, and the paper must report empirical false-commit rates under reuse rather than claim a guarantee.

The asymmetric disposition can be misread: researchers may see ADMIT_PROVISIONAL as 'no gate'; the benchmark must show it blocks harm quickly, or the design loses credibility with exactly the audience that would cite it.

Privacy and DLP: cassettes contain user prompts, code and secrets; a scrub failure or an over-eager share feature is a worse incident than any regression; local-only by default, provider-boundary rule, and no cross-user sharing in v1.

Vendor pre-emption: Anthropic (plugin eval) and OpenClaw (Workshop) could ship their own decision rules; Pawl's defensibility is cross-harness coverage, the neutral record profile, and the acceptor benchmark, none of which a single vendor is incentivized to build.

Operational canary false positives: scanner-style false positives without an override path convert a gate into a bypass incentive (hermes#94353); the false-block rate on the user's own benign edits must be a first-class reported metric.
open_questions: What fraction of real sessions are replayable to a terminal check across harnesses beyond Claude Code (measured so far: 7 sessions, 2,062 tool calls, one machine), and does that fraction rise if the recorder captures the user's test command explicitly at Stop time?

How stable is the incumbent self-replay noise floor across days and provider model updates, and what k and alpha does the observed per-task stability distribution justify? Is a floor keyed on model_served enough, or does the control arm need re-measurement on every model version?

How far do mechanical adherence predicates go before a cross-family judge is needed, and what is the judge's false-pass rate on 'followed' (Blind Curator's cliff at ~0.45 says retirement decisions cannot rest on it)?

How should observational pooled statistics from live sessions (confounded) be combined with paired replay evidence (unbiased but sparse) without overstating attribution — a kappa-style discount, or strictly separate labels?
Should the gate ever admit on rung-3 (judge-only) evidence for non-verifiable work (writing, research), or is human-on-the-loop the only honest disposition there?

Which Claude Code auto-memory writes are actually hookable via PreToolUse on the memory dir, and which arrive through internal paths that only the watcher can see? The same question for Codex Memories.
Does the dsh hook-protocol bridge preserve PostToolUse updatedToolOutput semantics so that served-result replay works under DSH, or does DSH need its own tools/post-execute replace path?

What is the right owner of the signing key for acceptance records (user, evaluator host, or both), and will the in-toto/OTel/EEE communities accept a learned-artifact-acceptance predicate alongside the tool-call-authorization predicates they are standardizing?

How much of the statistical machinery survives when tasks are non-exchangeable and arrive in a non-stationary stream (the user's work changes week to week) — is corpus rotation a fix or a new confound?

Can the same layer govern shared stores (SkillClaw groups, Hermes Skill Sync, ClawHub) via local re-verification on receivers' cassettes, and does that generalize to a federated merge protocol, or is per-environment forking the only honest answer?

Where is the line between 'candidate' and 'L4/L5 event' when an agent edits hooks, settings or the evaluator's config on its own machine — can the layer detect that mechanically in every harness, or only in those with typed surfaces?
